transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... well, it's a bit difficult to talk about. I just... I've been feeling lately like I don't really deserve the trust people put in me. I keep replaying these small clinical imperfections in my head. It just... it makes me feel like I might be a dangerous doctor. So, I thought I should come in.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress?
I don't... I wouldn't say I try to ignore them. I just... think about the mistakes because they happened. I'm not really trying to push anything away, if that's what you mean.
Do you feel compelled to do anything in response to these thoughts about clinical imperfections?
No... I don't think so. I just... I don't really do anything. Just sit with it, I guess.
Do these thoughts about clinical imperfections feel like they invade your mind without you wanting to think about them?
No, not really. I don't... I wouldn't use the word invade. It's just... they're my thoughts. I'm just thinking about what I actually did. It's not like they come out of nowhere.
Are these thoughts and feelings about your clinical imperfections affecting your daily life or work as a doctor?

I mean... I still go in. I'm still showing up to the clinic. But... I guess I've had to ask some of the others to cover my non-urgent admin stuff. I just... don't have the energy for it. And I don't really go out anymore. I avoid making plans. I just... I don't trust myself right now. My judgment. So yeah, I guess it's affecting things a bit.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
No... I haven't really noticed any changes. My weight is about the same, I think.
Do you feel anxious about making mistakes or being judged by others as a doctor?
No... I wouldn't say I feel anxious. It's not really about other people judging me. I just... no, I don't think it's anxiety.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time lately?
I don't... I wouldn't say I feel sad. No. I just... I don't really know. But not sad, no.
Do you think about these clinical imperfections at times when you're not actually working or thinking about work?
I... well, no, not really. I try to leave work at work. I don't really dwell on things like that when I'm at home.
Do you feel guilty about the clinical imperfections you've been thinking about?

I... I guess so. It's just... I feel like I don't deserve the trust people put in me. When I do think about them, I keep replaying these small clinical imperfections and... I don't know, it just feels like they prove I'm a dangerous doctor. That's... why I'm here, I suppose.
Do you feel like these thoughts about clinical imperfections are irrational or unrealistic?

I... no. I don't think they're unrealistic. Even when I go back and review the chart and... and there's no evidence of a bad outcome... I still believe it. I just keep thinking that some routine delay or... an imperfect message from me has quietly harmed a patient somewhere. And... I just know everyone will eventually discover it.
Do you feel distressed by these thoughts about clinical imperfections?
I... yeah. I guess so. It's... hard to deal with.
Do you feel like these thoughts about clinical imperfections are repeating in your mind in a way that you can't control?
I... I don't know. Maybe. They just... they're just there. I haven't really thought about whether I can control them or not.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are in line with your own beliefs about yourself?
I... I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't thought about it like that. I just... I just know the thoughts are there.

Do you think these thoughts about clinical imperfections would stop or significantly decrease if someone you trust, like a senior colleague, told you that your concerns are unfounded and you are a competent doctor?

I doubt it. Because... I check the charts. And even when there's nothing there, no evidence of a bad outcome... it doesn't change anything. I still just believe that... like, some routine delay, or a message I didn't write perfectly... that it quietly harmed the patient. And that everyone will eventually discover it. So... no. Someone just telling me I'm fine wouldn't really fix it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about clinical imperfections are a preoccupation that occupies a lot of time in your day?
I don't know if I'd call it a preoccupation... I just... I mean, I go to work. I do my job. The thoughts are just... around. I haven't really timed how much of the day they take up.
Do you think these thoughts about clinical imperfections are intrusive, meaning they enter your mind without you choosing to think about them?
I guess... yeah. They just kind of show up. I don't really try to think about it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about clinical imperfections are thoughts that you'd like to get rid of but can't?
I don't know. I mean... I haven't really tried to get rid of them. They're just... there. It's just how things are.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are consistent with how you see yourself as a person?
I'm not really sure. I haven't... I don't really analyze it like that. I just go in and do my job. I don't know how I see myself, honestly.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are in line with your own beliefs about yourself as a competent doctor?
I don't really know. I haven't... I don't spend a lot of time thinking about my competence like that. I just try to get through my shifts.
